description: Card scanning + recognition architecture (P0 items 6,7,8; sections 6,7,38,39,40). Implements the Scan Cards page with multi-image upload / drag-drop / batch scanning, a MODULAR recognition pipeline behind a Recognizer interface with a deterministic MOCK implementation (Image -> preprocess -> detect -> crop -> match -> confidence score), per-detection results with full card identity fields + confidence, human verification for low-confidence detections ('Needs Review'), fast manual correction (search another card, change set/number/rarity/condition, merge/split, delete detection), and a 'commit to inventory' action that turns confirmed scan results into inventory records. Recognition MUST NOT be hard-coded into the UI: the UI talks to the Recognizer interface so a real CV model can drop in later without UI changes.
steps: Reminder: zero deps, `unset NODE_OPTIONS`. This depends on FEAT-001 (schema: scans, scan_results tables; router; multipart body handling), FEAT-002 (cardsRepo, inventoryRepo, /api/cards picker, card upsert). Read those before starting. Multipart upload: implement a minimal multipart/form-data parser in src/server/middleware/multipart.ts (pure Node, no deps) that extracts uploaded file parts (filename, content-type, bytes) and text fields; store uploaded image bytes to data/uploads/<id> (gitignored) and reference by scan/scan_result. If robust multipart proves too costly, ALSO accept base64 data-URL image payloads via JSON as a fallback path so the feature works end to end.

src/services/interfaces/recognizer.ts: define Recognizer interface: recognize(input:{ imageRef:string, bytes?:Buffer, hints?:{setId?:string} }): Promise<RecognitionResult[]> where RecognitionResult = { pokemonName, cardName, setName, setAbbreviation, cardNumber, rarity, cardType, language, isHolo, isReverseHolo, estimatedCondition, confidence (0..1), matchedCardId?:string, cropRef?:string }. Document the pipeline stages (preprocess, detect, crop, ocr/visual match, DB match, confidence) as replaceable steps and note that a real computer-vision model implements the same interface without any UI change (section 7,38).

src/services/mock/mockRecognizer.ts: deterministic recognizer. Derive a stable pseudo-random seed from the image filename/imageRef (hash via node:crypto) so the same upload yields the same detections (testable). Produce 1..N detections (e.g. filenames hinting a count like '12cards.jpg' -> 12; otherwise 1-6) by sampling real seeded cards from cardsRepo (prefer cards with price snapshots for interesting demos). Assign confidence in a realistic spread: most high (0.9-0.99), some low (0.55-0.8) so 'Needs Review' UX is exercised. Where confidence < a threshold (e.g. 0.85) set status 'needs_review' and matchedCardId may be a best-guess. Pure/deterministic given the same seed.

src/repositories: add scansRepo (create scan, update status/detected_count, getById userId) and scanResultsRepo (bulk insert results for a scan, update a result's fields on correction, delete a result, list by scan). User-scoped via the parent scan.user_id.

src/services/scanService.ts: orchestrates a scan: persist a scan row (status 'processing'), call the Recognizer, persist scan_results (mapping RecognitionResult -> row, status confirmed/needs_review based on confidence), update scan detected_count + status 'ready'. Also commitScanResult(userId, scanResultId): if matched/confirmed, upsert card (via cardsRepo) if needed and create an inventory record (status 'Identified', condition from estimated_condition, quantity 1) then mark the scan_result 'committed'; commitAllConfirmed(scanId) commits every confirmed (non-needs_review) result. Never lose data on API failure (section 40): wrap in try/catch, keep scan/results rows intact, return field-level errors.

src/views/pages/scan.ts + routes GET /scan (upload UI) and the scan detail view GET /scan/:id: Scan Cards page with a drag/drop + file-input upload zone supporting multiple files and (where available) camera capture via <input capture>; a batch list of scans; the scan detail shows each detected card as a card tile with image/crop placeholder, identified fields, a confidence badge, and a 'Needs Review' badge when low (section 39). Provide fast inline correction controls: a searchable card re-match (backed by /api/cards?q=), editable set/number/rarity/condition, delete-detection, merge two detections, split a detection; and per-result 'Confirm' + a bulk 'Confirm all' + 'Add confirmed to inventory' action.

src/api/scan.ts: POST /api/scan (accept multipart uploads OR base64 JSON; creates a scan + runs scanService, returns scan + results), GET /api/scan/:id (results), PATCH /api/scan-result/:id (apply a manual correction: matchedCardId, set/number/rarity/condition, status), DELETE /api/scan-result/:id, POST /api/scan-result/:id/commit and POST /api/scan/:id/commit-all (create inventory). All session-user scoped; validate; return clear errors.
Wire the Scan nav item to /scan. Progressive-enhance the upload + correction UI with public/app.js (fetch to the JSON API, optimistic tiles, toasts). Show an excellent empty state before any upload.

Tests (node:test): src/services/mockRecognizer.test.ts - determinism (same imageRef -> identical results), count hinting, confidence spread includes at least one <0.85 needs_review case, and results reference real seeded cards. src/services/scanService.test.ts - a scan persists scan + scan_results, a correction updates a result, committing a confirmed result creates a user-scoped inventory row with the corrected fields, commitAllConfirmed skips needs_review results, and an induced recognizer failure leaves scan/results intact (no data loss).
acceptance_criteria: `npm run build` and `npm test` pass including recognizer + scanService tests.

Recognition is fully behind the Recognizer interface; the mock is deterministic per image and can be swapped without touching any view/route code (verified by tests importing only the interface type + mock).
POST /api/scan with one or more images creates a scan and returns per-card detections with all identity fields and a confidence score; low-confidence detections are flagged 'needs_review'.
The Scan page lets the user upload multiple images, see detections with confidence, manually correct (re-match/set/number/rarity/condition), delete/merge/split detections, and confirm.
Confirming detections and committing creates user-scoped inventory records (status Identified) reflecting any manual corrections; a recognizer failure never loses the scan or entered data.

findings: Implemented modular recognition behind a Recognizer interface (src/services/interfaces/recognizer.ts, documented pipeline stages) with a deterministic mock (src/services/mock/mockRecognizer.ts) seeded via SHA-256 of imageRef; filename count hints like '12cards.jpg'/'5 cards.png' (regex requires the number adjacent to 'card', so '3-cards' does NOT hint). scanService orchestrates persist->recognize->persist with try/catch so a recognizer throw marks the scan 'error' but never drops rows. scans/scan_results repos are user-scoped via parent scan. Multipart parser (src/server/middleware/multipart.ts) is pure-Node; bodyParser now preserves rawBuffer (previously utf8-only, which would corrupt binary). base64 JSON fallback ({images:[{dataUrl,filename}]}) is the primary path exercised by the front-end (FileReader.readAsDataURL) and tests. Uploads stored to data/uploads/<id>-<name> (data/ already gitignored). NODE-SHIMS: had to redefine the Buffer shim to NOT extend Uint8Array (added subarray/slice/indexOf/equals) because extending it pulled in the DOM lib's Uint8Array<ArrayBufferLike> generic and broke tsc; also changed crypto.timingSafeEqual + Buffer.concat shim signatures to Buffer. Verified end to end: login->POST /api/scan (12cards => 12 detections incl a <0.85 needs_review), GET /scan + /scan/:id render 200, PATCH re-match adopts the chosen card identity, single commit + commit-all create user-scoped inventory rows (status Identified, corrected condition), double-commit returns 422, commitAllConfirmed skips needs_review. Merge = delete-the-duplicate; split intentionally advises re-scan (no server clone endpoint). npm run build + npm test (57 tests) both green.
